statement: Yorùbá Ifẹ̀ creation traditions exist in multiple variants. Commonly documented versions begin with a primordial watery world and Olódùmarè commissioning creation; some emphasize Obàtálá, including the molding of human bodies from clay, while others give Odùduwà the decisive role in spreading earth over the waters and founding Ilé-Ifẹ̀. The variation is part of the evidence and should not be flattened into one canonical version.

does_not_demonstrate: Motif similarity with another tradition does not by itself demonstrate borrowing, common ancestry, or direct transmission.
notes: The claim distinguishes living oral variants from attempts to read those myths as literal chronicles of an ancient political conquest.
